headline: Tidal Cycle Access and Entry Requirements
reservation: Visitors must purchase a daily or annual Discovery Pass for entry; however, certain coastal activities are governed by the Bay of Fundy tide tables rather than a permit system. While park entry is generally available, roofed accommodations such as oTENTiks and campgrounds require advance booking through the Parks Canada reservation service. Always confirm the current tidal schedule as the shoreline accessible during low tide is submerged just hours later.

days.title: Tidal Fluctuations and Coastal Geology

stops.name: Point Wolfe
stops.detail: Cross the iconic red covered bridge to explore a site where a bustling logging community once met the sea.

stops.name: Herring Cove
stops.detail: Walk the seafloor at low tide to observe tidal pools and sea caves carved by the world's highest tides.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour of local travel; road speed limits are strictly enforced to protect local deer.
days.note: Consult the official tide table daily as access to the beach at Herring Cove changes by roughly an hour each day.

days.title: Highland Forests and River Valleys

stops.name: Dickson Falls
stops.detail: Follow the most popular boardwalk in the park through a lush, moss-covered valley to a cooling waterfall.

stops.name: Laverty Falls
stops.detail: Hike through the Acadian forest to reach a curtain-style waterfall and deep swimming holes in the Upper Salmon River.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; gravel interior roads may require slower speeds than paved sections.
days.note: The hike to Laverty Falls involves a steady climb on the return journey; allow sufficient time before dusk.

days.title: Panoramic Summits and Freshwater Lakes

stops.name: Matthew's Head
stops.detail: Traverse open fields and coastal forests for a high-vantage view over the Bay of Fundy's muddy flats.

stops.name: Bennett Lake
stops.detail: Relax at the park's primary freshwater lake, ideal for a calm paddle away from the turbulent bay waters.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; the route between the highland plateau and the coast is steep.
days.note: Fog can roll in quickly from the Bay, drastically reducing visibility on the highland roads.

intel.title: Village and Trailhead Limits
intel.text: Parking in the village of Alma can be difficult during peak weekend lunch hours. At Dickson Falls, the small lot fills quickly; consider visiting earlier in the morning or late afternoon.

intel.title: Valley Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service is generally reliable in Alma and the Chignecto North area, but drops significantly in the Point Wolfe and Laverty Falls valleys. Do not rely on streaming services for navigation in the park's western end.

intel.title: Gateway Provisions
intel.text: Fuel is available in the gateway village of Alma, but there are no stations within the park itself. Ensure you have a full tank if planning to explore the nearby Fundy Trail Parkway.

intel.title: Tide-Dependent Planning
intel.text: Schedule your visit to the 'mudflats' or sea caves within two hours of low tide. High tide occurs roughly every 12.5 hours and can trap unwary hikers against the cliffs.

intel.title: Winter Road Closures
intel.text: While Route 114 remains open, many internal park roads including the road to Point Wolfe are not plowed in winter. Access is limited to snowshoeing or skiing during the snowy months.

plan.arrival: Fly into Moncton (YQM) and drive approximately 90 minutes south, stopping in Riverview for major grocery supplies before reaching Alma.
plan.vehicle: Passenger cars are fine for main routes; however, check for seasonal weight restrictions on the Point Wolfe covered bridge if driving a large RV.
plan.goldenHour: Matthew's Head provides a panoramic sunset view over the Bay of Fundy, though coastal fog is a common seasonal variable.
